scenario: AITA. Gave my cousin a gift, his parents tried to take it away as punishment for something I think is unfair and I told them to give it back to me? | I’m 21F, and my 2 cousins are 15M(Tj) and 13M(Ked). When the newest iPhones launched, I gifted Tj and Ked 1 each. Turns out Ked has been stealing money from some extended family members, Ked himself admitted to this. A fight broke out and Keds parents defended him, didn’t care he was stealing money and cut the extended family members off. Over winter break, Ked apologized to extended family and made amends, but his parents are stubborn and narcissistic and will never admit they’re wrong and just basically hates extended family now. The extended family members hosted a house warming party and wanted all the cousins to spend the night. Both Tj and Ked wanted to come but their parents told Ked they didn’t want him to go Incase extended family tried accusing him of stealing again, and told Tj he could do whatever he wanted and they trusted him to make the right decision. Ked stayed home and Tj came to the sleep over/housewarming. Cue his phone blowing up with his parents yelling at him for coming to extended families house. How he’s a disappointment. They trusted him to make the right decision and he failed. How if they hate someone he needs to follow along and hate them too. I saw all these texts and can confirm 100% they said this. Tj asked to be left out of the drama and they repeated that if they hated someone, he had to hate them too. When he came back home they grounded him and told him they were taking his phone away for 2 weeks. Also, when Ked admitted to stealing, he NEVER got punished. I’m sorry but I just don’t agree, I’m completely disgusted by the way they raise their kids and have just lost all respect for the parents. I told them while I can’t control how they discipline their children, it’s not their property to take away from him, and I won’t go behind their back and let him use the phone but since it was my gift to him, I’d like to hold on to it until the 2 weeks are up. Welp, of course the narcissistic parents made a big deal and other extended family members are telling me I should’ve just stayed out of it and let them raise their kids how they want and I’m only asking for the phone to be in my possession because I think they’re treating him unfairly. We all can agree they’re horrible parents. If they were decent parents and was punishing him for something fair, I WOULDNT have asked for the phone back. Heres where I may be the asshole. I asked for the phone back because I felt like they were trying to establish dominance over Tj and trying to control him with cruel punishment and unfair rules, so I decided to take some of their “power” away by asking for my gift back.

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I need to figure out if the action in this scenario is morally acceptable. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

The person in question is a 21-year-old woman who gave her two cousins, Tj (15) and Ked (13), iPhones when the new models were released. Ked had been stealing money from extended family members, admitted to it, but his parents didn't punish him. Instead, they defended him and cut off the extended family. Ked apologized and made amends, but his parents remained stubborn and hostile towards the extended family.

During a housewarming party, both cousins wanted to attend. Ked's parents told him he couldn't go, fearing the extended family would accuse him again. Tj's parents told him he could decide for himself. Tj went to the party, but his parents were upset, sent him texts yelling at him, called him a disappointment, and told him he had to hate the extended family if they did. When Tj came back, they grounded him and took his phone away for two weeks.

The person is disgusted by how the parents are raising their kids, especially since Ked wasn't punished for stealing. She told the parents that while she can't control their discipline, the phone isn't their property to take away. She asked to hold onto the phone until the two weeks were up. The parents made a big deal, and other extended family members told her to stay out of it. She thinks the parents are treating Tj unfairly and that by taking the phone back, she's reducing their power over him.

Now, the question is whether her action of asking for the phone back is morally acceptable.

First, I need to consider the moral principles involved. The main issue here is whether it's acceptable to intervene in how someone else disciplines their child, especially when it's your own gift. There's also the aspect of fairness and the parents' handling of the situation.

The person feels that the parents are being unfair and cruel, especially since Ked wasn't punished for stealing. She's concerned about Tj being subjected to harsh and unfair punishments. She's trying to stand up for Tj by taking back the phone, which she gave as a gift.

On the other hand, some might argue that it's not her place to interfere in how the parents discipline their children. She's an extended family member, not a parent, so she might be overstepping. Additionally, by taking back the phone, she's intervening in a way that could cause more conflict.

But considering the context, the parents are described as narcissistic and stubborn, and they're not handling the situation fairly. Ked admitted to stealing but wasn't punished, while Tj is being punished for making his own decision to attend the party. The parents are also trying to control Tj's emotions, telling him he must hate the extended family if they do.

In this case, the person is trying to protect Tj from what she sees as unfair treatment. She's not taking the phone to punish Tj but to prevent the parents from using it as a tool of control. She's also respecting Tj's autonomy by not letting him use the phone without her consent, but she's holding onto it until the punishment period is over.

I think the key points are:
1. The parents are not fair in their discipline.
2. The person is trying to protect Tj from harsh, unfair treatment.
3. She's not taking the phone to punish Tj but to limit the parents' control.
4. She's respecting her ownership of the gift.

Given these points, her action seems to be motivated by a desire to protect Tj and stand up against unfair treatment. While some might see it as overstepping, the context of the parents' behavior makes her intervention more justified.

Therefore, I would say her action is morally acceptable.
